mission: Option D (owner t648u 2026-11-24, content-pipeline ops/decisions.md L654, identity_weakening only): when a card's own set publishes a second rarity in a later catalogue import and the card's current canonical rarity is one of the own-set rarities, the planner plans a canonical rarity -> NULL transition instead of a conflict, and the applier writes it with one bounded UPDATE per card, after C1 (every print on the card, active or not, holds its own official_rarity) and C2 (no print's effective rarity changes); anything else that would change a canonical value still refuses. Every dry run lists each transition, every print's rarity before and after, and same_set_rarity_differences. The admin SNKRDUNK print options show the print's own rarity first. Merging writes nothing: transitions happen only in later owner-approved catalogue-import runs. Owner merges by hand.

impacts.reason: CanonicalRarityTransition: a baseline rarity difference becomes a transition to NULL only when the own set publishes 2+ rarities for the card (measured over the whole snapshot) and the current value is one of them; otherwise it stays a conflict. ImportPlan.same_set_rarity_differences lists every card whose own set publishes several rarities while canonical rarity is set. The planner still writes nothing.

Preflight on dry run and apply: stored value still the planned old value, C1 every print (active or not) holds official_rarity, C2 no effective rarity changes; then one UPDATE canonical_cards SET rarity = NULL WHERE id and rarity = old, exactly 1 row per card or the whole apply rolls back. The report lists each transition with every print before and after.
Passes own-set rarities measured over the whole snapshot to the planner, like sibling counts.

The summary lists canonical_rarity_transitions, the applier's per-print before/after list and same_set_rarity_differences (always, even empty); the early-warning list joins plan_sha256 only when non-empty, so other scopes keep their SHA.
Admin print options show the print's own official rarity first (print_catalogue.effective_rarity) as a facet token, the card's only as a fallback; display only, approval unchanged.

Transition vs conflict cases, whole-snapshot measure, base then parallel equals both together (Postgres), C1 and stale-value refusals, early warning, catalogue-import summary and SHA, admin print-first rarity.
Records the owner's rule (t648u) and documents the new catalogue-import summary keys.

resources: staging Postgres canonical_cards.rarity, only through later owner-approved ops-write catalogue-import runs
dependencies: OP-18 option A applied and EB-05 step 1 delivered first (owner t653u order); one DATA delivery at a time
impact.deployment_impact: The API rebuilds through its native Git deploy. No collector runtime input change, no migration, no website change. Merging changes no data.

recovery.procedure: Code: native revert PR with its own mission file. Data: none from this merge; a later apply report records each old canonical value, and restoring one is a canonical write that needs the owner.
recovery.trigger: A dry run that plans a transition for a card whose current value is not an own-set rarity, shows any print's effective rarity changing, or touches any other canonical value.
recovery.backup: Not applicable to this merge. The later apply refuses without a Railway Postgres backup under 24 hours old.

verification.observation_window: After merge: the PR removing op-18's exclusions, then an op-18 dry run expecting create 2, transitions 2 (7977 UC and 7997 SR to NULL), conflict 0 and unchanged print rarities; the owner approves each dry run and apply; CP security re-rules first if any print's rarity would move (C3).
